messages:
jess: Noticing ~12-20% tail latency increase on host-side for short requests after runtime 2.3.1. Traces point to tokenization + parse + small chunk writes (~1-4 writes per stream).

kai: Dug in with `perf` and a flamegraph: https://perf.internal/graphs/6187 (sandbox). Hot path is parse_request -> tokenize_utf8 -> writev

omid: Did kernel selection change in 2.3.1? We shipped a new fused-attention preferred path for seq<=64 that might alter request paths.

jess: Yep — kernel selector now prefers fused kernel for short sequences. Unexpected side-effect: kv cache keys are generated with the new kernel id suffix; causes more kvcache lookups / misses for chat reuse.

paul: kvcache logs show miss rate jump from 8% -> 22% on canary for short sequences. Suspect normalization mismatch between old/new key format.

kai: Quick log snippet:
```
[ingress] req_id=abc123 parse_request 0.9ms
[tokenize] req_id=abc123 tokenize_utf8 1.8ms
[net] writev(3) bytes=512
```
We see more small writev calls after chunking change.

jess: Also found: grpc chunking change reduced chunk cap -> 512 bytes (was 2k). This increases syscalls and writev overhead. Reverting that alone drops syscalls ~40% in microbench.

omid: Batching heuristics may be compounding this — we reduced batch hold time to 1ms in the same release to lower latency, but combined with more syscalls it increases tail.

paul: Proposed action items:
- revert chunk cap change on canary
- add kv key normalization unit + integration tests
- emit telemetry for syscalls/writev per request

ci-bot: deploy-bot: Rolling revert of `chunk-cap-512` to canary pool (canary-1).. status: started :gear:

jess: I'll open a PR with the revert + a microbench harness. Quick numbers: baseline(2.2.x) median=22ms p95=48ms; after 2.3.1 median=26ms p95=59ms; after revert median=23ms p95=50ms.

kai: Added `--kv-key-v2` flag on staging run to correlate keys -> hit/miss. Will share correlation chart later.

paul: I'll add an alert to detect kvcache miss rate >15% for short requests.

jess: Thanks all :thumbsup: I'll send a short postmortem once the canary finishes.
